# testdata/vcs — git object-store fixtures

`internal/vcs` reads `HEAD`, the commit graph and the remote URL out of a git
repository **by parsing the object store**, never by executing `git` (decision
D-1). The fixtures are therefore repositories, and **none of them is checked
in.**

## Why nothing is checked in

1. **A hostile repository must not be a checkout hazard.** The most important
   fixture is a repository carrying a `.git/config` with `core.pager`,
   `core.fsmonitor`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.hooksPath`, `core.editor`,
   `alias.log`, `remote.origin.proxy` and `uploadpack.packObjectsHook` all
   naming a command that creates a sentinel file, plus executable hook scripts.
   Committing a nested `.git` directory full of that, into this repository, in a
   project whose whole subject is hostile packaging, would be indefensible — and
   `git` cannot even carry a nested `.git/` faithfully.

2. **`git` must not build the fixtures either.** A test that shells out to
   `git init && git commit` to produce a fixture makes the suite depend on the
   binary this package exists to avoid, and it hides the one thing worth
   pinning: that *these exact bytes* are the format the reader understands. So
   `internal/vcs/gitlog_test.go` writes the object store itself — zlib loose
   objects, a version-2 pack index, and packfiles containing whole objects,
   `REF_DELTA`s and `OFS_DELTA`s, with the delta instructions generated by the
   test's own encoder.

## The shapes the tests build

| Shape                                       | Expected answer                          |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| loose ref, packed ref, both                 | loose wins — git's own precedence        |
| detached HEAD, bare repository              | resolves                                 |
| unborn branch                               | `ErrNoRef`                               |
| `HEAD` → `refs/a` → `refs/b` → `refs/a`     | `ErrLimit`, bounded, no hang             |
| `HEAD` naming `../../etc/passwd`            | refused before any open                  |
| `HEAD` replaced by a symlink                | refused unresolved                       |
| `.git` as a **file** (`gitdir:` pointer)    | `ErrUnsupported` — pointer not followed  |
| `objects/info/alternates`                   | not followed; a coverage gap             |
| `extensions.objectformat = sha256`          | `ErrUnsupported`, not "corrupt"          |
| commits in a packfile                       | read (this is the real-world case)       |
| `REF_DELTA` + `OFS_DELTA` commit chains     | reconstructed                            |
| object stored under a name that is not its hash | `ErrCorrupt`                         |
| `OFS_DELTA` whose base offset is its own    | refused structurally, no hang            |
| delta chain deeper than the cap             | `ErrLimit`                               |
| pack index v1                               | `ErrUnsupported`, reported as a gap      |
| missing parent object                       | `ErrIncomplete` **with** the commits read |
| `[include] path = …` in `.git/config`       | not followed, and the error says so      |
| hostile config + hooks                      | correct answers, **and no sentinel**     |

## Live measurement

`TestLiveHelperClones` is skipped unless `AURVET_LIVE_VCS=1`. Measured
2026-08-05 against the 34 clones in the reference system's yay cache, with this
reader:

    clones=34 head-ok=34 remote-ok=34 log-ok=34 head-failed=0

Also measured on that population, and the numbers the limits are derived from:
largest packfile 577,037 B; largest pack index 60,432 B; most objects in one
pack 2,120; longest history 565 commits; longest commit message 1,706 B; 35
packs across 34 clones; **19 of 34 clones have an entirely empty loose object
store**, which is why packfile support is not optional; 8 of 34 contain merge
commits (50 in total), which is why the date-order caveat on `walk` is stated
rather than engineered around.
